[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Function-Based Views (FBVs) vs. Class-Based Views (CBVs) in Django"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django provides two primary ways to write views: Function-Based Views (FBVs) and Class-Based Views (CBVs). Understanding when and how to use each approach is essential for building scalable, maintainable web applications."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What are Function-Based Views (FBVs)?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"FBVs use Python functions to handle web requests and return HTTP responses. They are straightforward, highly explicit, and ideal for simple logic because you can see the entire execution path from top to bottom."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from django.shortcuts import render, get_object_or_404
from .models import Article

def article_list(request):
    articles = Article.objects.all()
    return render(request, 'blog/article_list.html', {'articles': articles})"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"What are Class-Based Views (CBVs)?"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"CBVs encapsulate view logic inside Python classes rather than functions. Django provides a rich set of generic class-based views for common tasks like listing, creating, updating, and deleting objects, promoting code reuse through inheritance and mixins."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from django.views.generic import ListView
from .models import Article

class ArticleListView(ListView):
    model = Article
    template_name = 'blog/article_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'articles'"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Differences and When to Use Them"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Readability: FBVs are often easier for beginners to read because all control flow is visible in one place without jumping across parent classes."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Code Reusability: CBVs excel at DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principles through mixins and generic views, allowing you to implement CRUD operations with minimal code."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Extensibility: CBVs can be easily customized by overriding specific methods, whereas FBVs rely heavily on conditional statements (like checking request.method == 'POST')."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Neither approach is objectively better than the other. Use FBVs for simple, highly customized views where explicit logic is preferred. Use CBVs for standard CRUD operations and when you want to leverage Django's built-in generic views for rapid development."}]
